title: Auditing a Psychology Paper for Open Science & Replicability Indicators
description: Evaluate an empirical psychology research article against modern Open Science criteria.
problemStatement:
The Open Science movement emerged to counteract p-hacking, publication bias, and small sample sizes that sparked the Replication Crisis.

### Instructions:
Conduct a methodology audit of an empirical psychology paper using the Open Science Badges framework:

1. **Preregistration Check**: Did the authors preregister their directional hypotheses, sample size justification (power analysis), and exclusion criteria before data collection?
2. **Open Data & Code**: Are the raw anonymized datasets, analysis scripts (R/Python), and experimental stimuli publicly hosted on OSF or GitHub?
3. **Sample Size & Power**: Was the statistical power adequate (e.g. $1 - \beta \ge 0.80$) to detect subtle effect sizes without inflation?
4. **Transparency Rating**: Assign an overall replicability confidence rating (High, Moderate, Fragile) and explain your reasoning in 2 paragraphs.
hints: Hint 1: Studies with tiny sample sizes (N < 30 per condition) reporting p-values hovering just below .05 (e.g. p = .048) are classic warning signs of p-hacking.
Hint 2: Registered Reports offer the highest gold standard of replicability because peer review occurs prior to data collection.
